newsitem.title: GERMANY: Missing millionaire kidnapped by Germans-police.
newsitem.headline: Missing millionaire kidnapped by Germans-police.

text.p: Police probing the abduction of German multi-millionaire Jakub Fiszmann said on Tuesday it was more likely to be the work of a German criminal gang rather than the Russian mafia or other international terrorists.
Police said the search for Fiszmannn, 40, continued on Tuesday, with 25 police officers searching a former arms depot near Frankfurt for clues.
The Fiszmanns, one of the richest families in Germany, offered a one-million-mark ($650,000) reward late on Monday for information about the whereabouts of the missing businessman.
Police in Wiesbaden said they hoped the reward would lead to clues to help free Fiszmann. They had received around 180 tip-offs from the public relating to the case so far.

Based on their investigations so far, the police said they thought the kidnappers were German. There had been speculation in the media that Fiszmann had been kidnapped by the Russian mafia or another terrorist organisation.
Fiszmann's brother Georg paid over a four-million mark ransom on October 10 for his release, but his kidnappers failed to free him as promised the following day.
At the weekend police said they believed that Fiszmann was still alive and being held near Frankfurt.
Police have spent recent days scouring the countryside around Idstein, north of Frankfurt, where the ransom had been paid out, but said they had as yet found no concrete clues.
Searchers used helicopters and tracker dogs to comb the area after an anonymous phone call said cars had been seen in the area, which police said might have been involved.
They were also looking for dug-outs in the ground which could be used to hide Fiszmann.
Fiszmann needs medication to treat specific food allergies and police said they were watching out for sales of certain drugs.
The last confirmation that Fiszmann was alive came on October 2, one day after his abduction during which he was injured in a scuffle.
Fiszmann telephoned a contact person, believed to be his girlfriend, saying he was being held by kidnappers in a cellar.
A ransom of 3.5 million marks was set, but was later raised to four million marks.
Police confirmed reports at the weekend that the Fiszmann family had total assets exceeding 400 million marks. ($1=1.5374 Mark)
